ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-59 and R.561-1 to R.561-34 of the French Code monétaire et financier implementing EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; Articles L.561-46 to L.561-50 CMF and Article R.561-1 CMF (French beneficial owner register incorporated in the Registre National des Entreprises) introduced by Decree No. 2020-118 of 12 February 2020 and Ordinance No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020; Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); Article 1835 of the Code civil and Article L.223-1-1 of the Code de commerce (UBO clause in statuts); EU Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds; CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 in joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 (restricting general public access to the UBO register and limiting access to competent authorities and legitimate-interest persons).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent corporate authority of the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (France is party to the 1961 Apostille Convention) or Consular Legalization for non-convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration) appointing the French gérant and attorneys-in-fact for incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Duly authorized shareholder or board resolution of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization in the issuing jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copies of official identity documents (passports) of all beneficial owners, the proposed gérant, and the legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority plus notarial certification in the holder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable to the country of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign commercial register or equivalent authority in the UBO's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank seal and officer signature certified by apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, gérant, and proposed service providers against: (i) French TRACFIN typology guidance and AML/CFT directives; (ii) the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iii) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iv) the OFAC SDN List as a best-practice cross-check; and (v) the French domestic PEP database covering public office-holders, their family members, and close associates under Article L.561-10 CMF. The appointed AML compliance officer must apply customer due diligence per Articles L.561-5 to L.561-10 CMF, enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk third States, and must decline the engagement or file a suspicious transaction report to TRACFIN under Article L.561-15 CMF upon any confirmed screening hit. A fresh screening pass is mandatory within 24 hours before execution of the statuts.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); public RCS/name search via data.inpi.fr and infogreffe.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All constitutive documents must be in French pursuant to Article L.223-6 of the Code de commerce and Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994 (Loi Toubon). The corporate name may contain Latin-script foreign words; where the desired name originates from a non-Latin script, it must be transliterated into Latin characters and the transliterated form also recorded in the statuts and the RNE file. The name must be distinctive, non-deceptive, and compatible with the SARL legal form.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Crédit, Assurance, Mutuelle, Caisse d'Épargne (regulated financial terms requiring prior ACPR or ministerial authorization)
Avocat, Notaire, Huissier de Justice, Commissaire aux Comptes, Expert-Comptable (regulated professional titles reserved to licensed practitioners and firms)
France, République, National, Office National, Institut de France (sovereign-emblem and public-entity terms requiring concession or otherwise prohibited)
Croix-Rouge, Nations Unies, Union Européenne, UNESCO (protected international emblems and institutional names)
Misleading suffixes such as Société Anonyme or SA when the actual legal form is SARL
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No separate administrative name-reservation exists for SARLs; name protection accrues at RNE registration. Upon rejection by the INPI/RNE: (i) within 15 days, counsel files a written motion for reconsideration (recours gracieux) with INPI, attaching distinctiveness and trademark search evidence; (ii) if rejected, an administrative appeal may be filed within 30 days of notification, or judicial action brought before the competent Tribunal judiciaire for INPI name decisions and before the competent Tribunal de commerce for greffe/RCS refusals under Articles R.123-80 et seq. of the Code de commerce; (iii) a parallel remedy is immediate filing of an alternative name and, where a trademark conflict exists, an opposition under Article L.712-4 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle. The rejected name may not be commercially used pending final resolution.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally accepted: a SARL must maintain a registered office in France (Article L.123-10 Code de commerce). Domiciliation through a state-approved business domiciliation company under Article L.123-11-2 of the Code de commerce is permissible and is a standard market practice for tax-consulting firms. However, a purely nominal virtual office with no identifiable local management, no physical file retention, and no decision-making presence substantially increases the risk of adverse characterization under the French abuse of law doctrine (abus de droit, Article L.64 of the Livre des procédures fiscales) and under OECD BEPS substance requirements for transfer pricing and tax advisory activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: annualized 10-15% probability for a newly formed low-risk advisory SARL. Announced corporate tax audits (vérification de comptabilité) are the standard inspection route; unannounced URSSAF social security inspections and DGCCRF commercial checks may occur. Maintaining a physically open and appropriately staffed registered office during business hours materially mitigates inspection risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs de la Société à Responsabilité Limitée
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of €1 fully paid-up upon subscription; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION
The undersigned, acting as the Board of Directors of the proposed Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) [Company Name], hereby resolve unanimously as follows:
1. To approve the subscription of all shares in the capital of the Company by [Shareholder Name], representing 100% of the shares, with the nominal capital fixed at one Euro (€1.00), fully subscribed and paid up in cash.
2. To adopt the registered office of the Company at [Full Address], France, and to authorize the filing of the articles of association with the competent registry authority.
3. To appoint [Full Name] as President and Managing Director (Président) of the Company, with full powers of representation and management, and to grant all necessary delegations.
4. To approve the draft articles of association presented, which shall be executed by the President.
5. To authorize the President to proceed with the statutory incorporation formalities, including submission of documents to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and obtaining the SIREN number.
This resolution is adopted by unanimous consent of the Board on [Date].

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities establishing a French SARL must obtain a SIREN number through guichet-entreprises.fr or directly with DGFiP; subsequent VAT identification follows mandatory registration protocols
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No broad check-the-box elections; limited options include micro-entreprise regime for small businesses and hybrid mismatch adjustments under EU directives

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 85,000 EUR (general turnover threshold); 30,000 EUR for intra-EU acquisitions and services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing (e-facturation) for B2B transactions since October 2024 with API integration to the fiscal authority platform and digital stamping for clearance

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods outside the EU and qualifying cross-border services; requires proof of actual export and non-domestic use
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Proof of delivery to non-EU destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Administrative penalties up to 80% of the VAT amount, plus interest and potential criminal sanctions for fraudulent zero-rating claims

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) for external financial relations and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) for banking supervision and payment services authorisation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a founding member of the euro area and applies no general currency convertibility restrictions under Article 63 TFEU on free movement of capital. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible between EUR and foreign currencies through authorised resident credit institutions. There are no exchange control licences, no prior approval requirements for profit remittances, and no substantive statutory hurdle to dividend distributions, shareholder loan repayments, or trade payments. Practical impediments are limited to regulatory-compliance duties: French banks must transmit balance-of-payments (BOP) statistics to Banque de France for cross-border flows, verify economic purpose under AML/KYC rules, and apply sanctions and embargo screening. Profit remittance by a French SARL is consequently constrained not by FX restriction but by corporate-law solvency tests, shareholder approval formalities, and French dividend withholding tax / parent-subsidiary directive eligibility where the recipient is an EU resident corporate shareholder.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. French and EU rules impose no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. The mandatory conversion rate is therefore 0%, and exporters may invoice in EUR or any freely convertible foreign currency, hold the proceeds in an account abroad or in France, and use them without approval. The only reporting obligation is indirect: the resident French bank records cross-border receipts in the balance-of-payments data collection of Banque de France for statistical purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for a French or EU/EEA regulated Electronic Money Institution (EMI) holding an ACPR authorisation or using PSD2 passporting into France, provided it offers French IBAN-bearing operational accounts and can support cross-border wires. Medium for a pan-EU EMI with no French physical branch, because transaction limits and clearing-rail access may be narrower and capital-deposit escrow services are rarely available. Low / not viable for an offshore digital EMI outside the EU/EEA: it cannot lawfully provide payment services to a French SARL, has no access to French payment schemes, does not hold a Banque de France settlement account, and creates disproportionate AML/CTF and sanctions risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no blanket statutory mandate that all directors appear physically in branch. French AML/KYC rules under the Monetary and Financial Code permit remote onboarding using ACPR-aligned video identification, eIDAS electronic signatures, notarised ID-certified copies, and independent source-of-funds verification. In practice, Tier-1 French banks will normally require at least one recorded video or structured telephonic interview with the legal representative and, for non-resident directors or complex international shareholding structures, may request a physical or diplomatic notarisation of identity. For the capital escrow account, the bank will verify the subscriber/shareholder and the legality of the capital deposit before issuing the bank certificate required for SARL registration with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory as the stated commercial purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed engagement letter defining boutique tax consultancy (ISIC 7020), evidence of registered statutory licence or regulated professional status (e.g. avocat or expert-comptable subject to an Ordre), professional indemnity insurance certificate, CVs and credentials of the directors, and a written statement confirming no tax evasion, no shell activity, and full substance in France.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or shareholders controlling a French SARL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passports and proof of residence of all directors and 25% beneficial owners, tax residence certificates, local police/regulatory background checks, corporate extract or shareholder register, source-of-wealth documentation for each material shareholder, and a clear explanation of the legitimate tax structuring role of any non-French entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered or offshore holding chain without transparent economic rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full organisational chart identifying every ultimate beneficial owner under the French UBO register obligation (Décret n° 2014-1284), corroborating commercial agreements, audited or certified financial statements for intermediate holding entities, and transfer pricing documentation prepared under OECD and French tax rules (article L.13 AA of the French Tax Code).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High expected cross-border receipts and repeated FX or treasury transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury policy, annual budget and cash-flow forecast, underlying client contracts and invoices, documented purpose for each major inbound/outbound transaction, confirmation that all transactions relate to bona fide advisory services, and a commitment to provide periodic transaction justifications on request to the French bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from a foreign shareholder raising source-of-funds doubts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarised or certified shareholder resolution approving the capital contribution, bank statements from the remitting shareholder showing a lawful origin of funds, evidence of the deposit of cash with a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and the legal share-capital subscription certificate issued for the SARL.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols require the foreign shareholder to transmit the capital injection by SWIFT MT103 through a reputable overseas bank to the French SARL's account at a Tier-1 French bank. The beneficiary account must be stated using the French IBAN (FR76 with the appropriate BIC), the transaction must include a transparent purpose code such as ISO 20022 purpose 'INTR' (intra-group capital transaction) or an equivalent corporate treasury code, and the remittance information must state 'Capital increase under French Commercial Code / souscription et libération du capital'. The French bank will verify the subscriber, screen against sanctions and PEP lists, confirm the consistency of the amount with the capital resolution, and issue or recognise the 'certificat de dépôt des fonds' required by the incorporation process. For amounts constituting foreign direct investment, the resident bank reports the BOP category to Banque de France; no prior administrative authorisation is required, but the French SARL must retain the board/shareholder resolution, subscriber identification records, and bank certificate to evidence clean source of funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EUR disbursements within the EEA, the SARL should use SEPA Credit Transfer, settled through TARGET2, with the counterparty's IBAN and invoice reference. For non-EEA or multi-currency disbursements, the SARL should use SWIFT MT103 with a UETR tracking reference, clearly stating the purpose code (e.g. 'TRAD' for trade payable or the relevant ISO 20022 code) and the invoice number, with charges arranged as 'SHA' or 'OUR' depending on vendor requirements. For larger trade settlements in goods-related transactions, a Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the French bank by SWIFT MT700/MT707 under UCP 600 is a recognised clearing rail, complemented by documentary collections or bank payment undertakings; the SARL's treasury should maintain a sufficient EUR and foreign-currency liquidity buffer to cover settlement date mismatches and fees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX outright forwards (EUR vs foreign currency) with a credit institution or investment firm
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or low-liquidity currencies where physical delivery is impractical
FX swaps (FXS) combining spot and forward legs
Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) for asset-liability alignment on cross-border investments
EUR/foreign-currency options (call/spread and put/spread) with documented underlying commercial exposure
Combinations of the above executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or French master derivative documentation, subject to EMIR clearing, margin and trade-reporting obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts approval by the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; no governmental filing at approval stage
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve accounts may lead to judicial injunction and daily penalties. It does not create an automatic fixed-date administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts and applicable management documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce) through the French business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; two months when filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine generally up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat offences within five years; judicial injunction and daily penalties may apply. No automatic strike-off is triggered solely by one late filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return, Form 2065 and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second working day after 1 May for a financial year ending on 31 December; generally within three months after the financial year-end for other closing dates, subject to the applicable e-filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge and late-payment interest calculated at the statutory monthly rate; aggravated penalties may apply for non-compliance or deliberate underreporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT annual reconciliation and periodic VAT returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly VAT returns according to the applicable regime; annual CA12 return generally due within three months after the end of the relevant period for the simplified regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment generally attracts a 10% surcharge and statutory late-payment interest; further assessments and penalties may apply for omissions or inaccurate returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally payable by 15 December each year; no annual return is normally required unless taxable facts change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment may generate a 5% surcharge and statutory late-payment interest; collection measures may follow continued non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information update, if ownership or control information changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French business formalities portal and Commercial Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Promptly after the change and generally within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurate beneficial ownership information may result in formal notice, court-ordered compliance, criminal penalties, and possible restriction or refusal of registration services. There is no routine annual confirmation filing where no information has changed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory when the SARL exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at the relevant financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional appointment rules may apply to certain parent, subsidiary, or controlled-company structures.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (Autorité des normes comptables). IFRS is generally relevant to qualifying consolidated accounts and is not the default framework for standalone SARL accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require a separate annual UBO confirmation where the registered information remains unchanged. The SARL must monitor ownership and control continuously, update the beneficial ownership filing after a change, and record share transfers in the corporate records. A qualifying transfer may also require registration tax formalities, amendment of corporate information, and registry filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or shareholders (registre des associés/share ledger)
Register of Managers and current corporate officer information
Minute book and signed records of shareholder decisions
Share transfer instruments and supporting ownership documentation
Annual accounts, accounting records, and applicable auditor reports

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-2,000 per year, depending on location, mail handling, domiciliation, and administrative services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,200-9,000 for a small SARL subject to statutory audit; higher for cross-border groups, consolidation, transfer pricing, or complex regulated activities

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
